svg.title: One knowledge base, four type structures, one backend, one decision ladder
svg.desc: A HyperX support article with its category, tags and PDF, shown as a Webflow Collection item, a Shopify metaobject, a Rust struct and a Jekyll page, with when each checks its shape and how each keeps a private article out. A table maps every field across the four structures to its Xano record field, what the Cloudflare Worker returns, and its single owner. Five Worker functions serve the search page and the chatbot, each with its check. An RMA decision ladder shows the chatbot climbing from knowledge-base answers to lookup to opening an RMA, with the conditions that escalate to a person, and a safety path that escalates immediately.
svg.text: TYPE STRUCTURES · PERMISSIONS · CRM SYNC KNOWLEDGE BASE
One knowledge base, four type structures, one backend
A HyperX support article (FAQ, category, tags and PDF) as each system types it, served to the search page and the chatbot. Values are examples.

svg.text: When does the shape get checked?
The earlier a model refuses a bad record, the fewer bad pages ship and the less the chatbot can quote.
EARLIER
LATER, OR NEVER
Rust: compile
bad code never builds
Shopify: write
bad data never saves
Webflow: save / publish
required fields only
Jekyll: build
only if you add the check
Mapped across all four, onto one backend
Xano holds the record. The Cloudflare Worker is the only way out and decides what each function returns. Every field has one writer.
TYPE STRUCTURES
BACKEND · RECORD → GATE → OWNER
Worker functions behind the search page and the chatbot, each with its check
The page and the <crm-chat> embed hold no rule and no key. Paths and cap names are illustrative; caps follow plane:resource:verb.

svg.text: The RMA decision ladder: when the chatbot hands over to a person
Each rung is a permission, not a script. The chatbot climbs while the rules hold; money moves only on a person's grant. Conditions are examples.

svg.text: The escalation record holds no name, email or phone: it links to the customer by ID, so the question can become training data without becoming personal data.
In bold: is_private. The live search page publishes data-is-private-article on every item; all 31 read "false" today. The flag itself is public, so the filter
has to run before publishing and in every Worker query, never in the browser. Tiers from "The AI ladder" (book 3.32); RMA conditions and cap names are hypothetical.
